questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A good academic environment. The possibility to live abroad and explore a country that i normally would not travel to just for holiday purposes, due to the great distance (Australia).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a very good experience, but the work load was so high that it was challenging to explore the country a bit more.

questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *

Additional comments
questions.answer: read above

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to find something affordable.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very pricy to live in Australia these days. Look for a flat in good time and try to find somebody who can assist you with recommendations about the districts, mobility etc.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was often a bit chaotic and it took them around a month to answer each of my emails, which was too slow for time sensitive matters such as visa.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I cannot remember it in detail. It was complicated.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were only the administration officers. It took them a month per email to answer, which was too slow for time sensitive matters such as visa.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Most worked out, but only because I did it myself BEFORE i was instructed to register courses (!!!). When I registered a week after the opening, I found that one of the desired courses was already booked out. However, I was officially told to register courses around a month later, which would have been way too late for many of the courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find somebody who has booked courses before and ask for help. Book right after opening. Do not wait until the administration officers tell you to register, otherwise it will be too late for many courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was excellent.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were more challenging than on KU. There were more deadlines and reports to deliver. It was definitely more busy than on KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Read above.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Urban Environmental Systems
- Earth Systems
- Environmental Data Analytics (EDA)
- Land Degradation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the above, but especially EDA, which levels quantitative skills, environmental analysis and gives a nice introduction to the programming language R at the same time.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Nationalparks, rent a camper and drive around. Explore the coast, but dont miss out on the Hinterlands!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the labs and lectures. Ask people to go to unibar after the lessons.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Australians are very easy going. However, I was shocked that the same applies for environmental matters. Climate change is a big topic, but nobody responds to it. Advice from Europeans are not really appreciated because they don't deem any of it to be applicable to Australia.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are very easy going.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Prepare in good time. The process is VERY time intensive. 
Find a buddy already before you go (LinkedIn?)
Studying is very different from KU. Be ready to have less group work and more responsibility yourself.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
- The workload is higher and there is less group work. 
- The examination is continuously. Instead of one final examination, there are multiple smaller assessments.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: A field trip in 'Land Degradation'. Good friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The deadlines. At some point i had to write 5 reports at the same time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
